title: Throughput reservations and staged failover for dedicated regional fleets
creator: Laura Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a mechanism for reserving committed throughput for Dedicated customers across regional and multi-zone fleets that also supports a staged failover model which preserves data residency guarantees. The feature combines per-customer throughput leases, zone affinity weights (soft-sticky placement), and a cold->warm->hot failover sequence so that we can meet throughput SLAs while minimizing cross-region data movement and avoiding noisy neighbor effects.

Background and Motivation:
- Customers running Dedicated pools pay for reserved capacity and expect predictable throughput and failover behavior. Current placement is best-effort and reactive when a zone/region degrades, which can cause sudden cross-region traffic bursts and violates residency constraints for regulated customers.
- We must support: guaranteed throughput windows (reservation profiles), configurable failover tiers (cold/warm/hot), and residency-enforcement that prevents routing requests outside allowed regions unless explicitly overridden in an emergency.

Proposed Design (high-level):
1) Throughput Reservations (capacity leases):
   - Each Dedicated customer can carve a reservation profile: a guaranteed tokens-per-second and a burst quota for short bursts. Internally we implement this as a token-bucket quota attached to the customer's routing policy.
   - Reservations map to pool slots across zones using a weight vector [z1:0.7, z2:0.2, z3:0.1] called soft-sticky placement. The orchestrator will prefer the primary zones but will allocate from secondary zones within configured thresholds.

2) Staged Failover (cold -> warm -> hot):
   - Cold: pre-provisioned but idle buffer lanes in allowed zones. No cross-region movement; used when a zone has transient capacity shortage.
   - Warm: partially populated replicas that can be ramped up within 30s; accepts traffic only for customers who have warm-failover enabled.
   - Hot: full failover to alternate region only when explicit runbook is triggered or when SLA breach imminent and residency override permitted. Hot failover requires audit logging and an opt-in residency override flag in the customer's contract.

3) Residency Enforcement and Compliance: 
   - Residency locks: metadata on customer profiles that lists allowed regions and disallowed regions. Routing decisions consult locks as an immutable policy except during a documented emergency workflow.
   - Audit trail: every cross-region decision is logged with reason, timestamp, and approver. Logs are shippable to customer audit sinks when requested.

4) Autoscaler Integration and Admission Control:
   - The autoscaler recognizes reserved throughput and pre-allocates buffer lanes proportionally. Scaling actions honor reservation priorities and attempt to satisfy reservations before scheduling best-effort workloads.
   - Admission control rejects new non-reserved work when cluster pressure threatens compliance with reservation SLAs.

5) Operational Controls and Operator UI:
   - Console exposes per-customer reservation profile, zone affinity weights, failover tier, and a simulated failover preview (estimated latency and ingress/egress costs).
   - Emergency override workflow in Console with two-person approval for cross-region fails.

Trade-offs and Rationale:
- Soft-sticky weighting reduces churn by keeping most traffic in preferred zones, but may increase tail latency when primary is degraded. The staged approach limits how much traffic can shift at each stage to keep latency and cost predictable.
- Pre-provisioning buffer lanes increases cost for idle capacity; we balance this with a tiered pricing model and adjustable buffer sizes per customer.
- Strict residency enforcement can prolong SLA breaches if alternate regions are off-limits. We provide an emergency override to reduce outage windows for enterprise customers with signed waivers.

Telemetry and SLOs to track:
- Reservation fulfillment rate (percentage of reserved throughput delivered per minute)
- Time to warm (median/90/99 p50/p90/p99)
- Percentage of requests using cold/warm/hot lanes
- Number of residency-override events and time to approve
- Impact on best-effort tenant latency under pressure

Rollout Plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): internal-only reservations for a handful of pilot customers in one region. Add detailed telemetry and circuit-breakers. (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (beta): expose Console controls and allow customers to opt-in. Limit to customers with residency set to regional only. (4 weeks)
- Phase 3 (GA): full automation, SLA-backed reservations, and optional buffer pricing. (8 weeks)

Runbook and Emergency Procedures:
- If a zone shows sustained packet loss + 20% CPU+ memory pressure and reservation fill drops below threshold, initiate staged failover: enable cold buffers, then scale warm lanes, then notify on-call before hot failover.
- Hot failovers require two approvers and must attach an audit log entry and communication to affected customers.

Open Questions and Next Steps:
- Default pricing for buffer lanes and how to expose cost estimates in Console.
- How to expose fine-grained residency toggles (per-route vs per-customer).
- Backpressure signals between runtime (kernel-level) and autoscaler to prevent overscheduling.

acceptance_criteria: Reservations can be created via API and Console and persist across orchestrator restarts
Autoscaler pre-allocates buffer lanes based on reservation profiles in canary region
Staged failover sequence (cold->warm->hot) exercises without violating residency lock for pilot customers
Telemetry shows reservation fulfillment >= 95% for pilot customers under normal degradation scenarios
Emergency override requires two approvals and writes an audit entry
